findings.title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts async work and immediately returns. getCalendar is now async (it awaits a dynamic import) and deleteMeeting is async, but nothing awaits the forEach callbacks, and the values they return (including calendar.deleteEvent) are discarded. The try/catch around forEach cannot see rejections from those callbacks. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletions may not have started. On a serverless runtime the process can freeze after the handler returns, so the old calendar event and video meeting are left in place after the booking is already marked CANCELLED, and failures surface only as unhandled rejections.

findings.title: WipeMyCal reschedule cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: Same control-flow bug as the Vital reschedule handler: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not wait for getCalendar, calendar.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. Because getCalendar now awaits a dynamic app import before deleteEvent is even called, the deletion often has not started when this function sends the reschedule email and returns true. The surrounding try/catch does not catch async failures. Result: the booking is cancelled in the database while the external calendar event and video meeting can remain, blocking the slot and leaving a stale invite.

findings.title: requestReschedule returns before integrations are deleted
findings.body: requestReschedule marks the booking CANCELLED, then uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and call deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await those promises, and the mutation continues straight into sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, then resolves. Callers therefore observe success before calendar and video teardown has run. With getCalendar and deleteMeeting now async, the external API calls are no longer even initiated synchronously, so a short-lived server handler can exit first and leave the original event on the calendar and the video meeting alive.

findings.title: Cancelling remaining recurring events drops calendar deletes
findings.body: When all remaining recurring instances are cancelled and a credentialId is present, calendar deletion is done with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). The async callbacks are never joined. Later, await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) runs while apiDeletes is still empty, because pushes happen only after getCalendar and deleteEvent resolve inside the detached callbacks. Those pushes also store settled results, not in-flight promises, so they cannot be tracked. Recurring bookings are marked CANCELLED and cancellation email is sent, but the external calendar events for those instances are not reliably deleted; import or API errors become unhandled rejections. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of and pushes the delete promise before awaiting; this branch needs the same treatment.
